topic: Grief at Christmas (companion Reel, off grid, still frames)
caption:
Most of us carry a timetable for grief. By the first Christmas, there is often a quiet sense that things should be settling.

A study of older widowed adults found distress rose around meaningful dates, such as a late partner's birthday and the holidays. How much it hurts on one day tells you very little. The shape of grief across months tells you more.

The short version of this week's carousel. The full carousel is on our profile @equal_psychology, and the full article is linked in bio.

Research:
Carr, D., Sonnega, J., Nesse, R. M., & House, J. S. (2014). Do special occasions trigger psychological distress among older bereaved spouses? An empirical assessment of clinical wisdom. The Journals of Gerontology: Series B, 69(1), 113-122. https://doi.org/10.1093/geronb/gbt061

This content is for general informational purposes and does not constitute psychological advice. Grief can be very personal. If you are experiencing significant distress, please speak with a registered health professional, or call Lifeline on 13 11 14.
